title: An orphan row in another case than a declared row cannot be adopted
body:
## Summary
A take filed under "ambient" while the declared row is "Ambient" draws an orphan row whose only act, adopt, is refused: the case-fold rule of arrangeGroups.ts and the exact match of rowsFor disagree.

## Description
arrangeGroups.ts:262-264 says names compare case-folded, so "Ambient" and "ambient" are one row, and addGroup (arrangeGroups.ts:285) refuses a case variant. rowsFor (packages/ui/src/components/audio/arrange.ts:103-111) compares a head's group to the declared list exactly, so a take carrying "ambient" is drawn as an orphan row beside "Ambient". RowHead's orphan chip sends {op:"add"} (packages/ui/src/components/audio/RowHead.tsx:127), which addGroup refuses with "“ambient” is already a row" - the row's only act is a dead press. A take reaches that spelling through ingest meta (lib/sound/takes.ts:329 `group: str(meta.group, 80)`) or the take PATCH (lib/sound/takes.ts:407). Fixed looks like: adopting a case-variant orphan files its takes under the declared spelling in the same store transaction (carriedBy, arrangeGroups.ts:343) and leaves the rows list as it is.

## Flow
- ingest or PATCH a kept take with group "ambient" while groups.music is ["Ambient"]
- the board draws rows Ambient, ambient (orphan), ungrouped
- press adopt on "ambient" -> applyGroupOp(add) -> {ok:false, error:"“ambient” is already a row"}
- fix: an adopt whose name folds onto a declared row is a merge - carriedBy re-files every take of the kind whose group is the orphan spelling to the declared one; the door (lib/sound/arrange.ts:104-117) already applies carried takes in one transaction

## Expected impact
The operator sees one row per name and the orphan's adopt works; today the cards must be dragged out one by one. Could break: an "add" typed in the new-row field that folds onto an existing row must still be refused (only an orphan adopt merges).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one row per case-folded name, and an orphan's adopt reaches it
Before: probe (tsx over arrange.ts/arrangeGroups.ts): rowsFor(["Ambient"], [take group "ambient"]) -> 3 rows incl. orphan "ambient"; applyGroupOp add "ambient" -> refused; orphan rows with a working act 0 of 1
After: predicted 1 of 1 (orphan adopt merges, 0 orphan rows after)
Method: probe for Before; After not taken - the fix spans arrangeGroups.ts, RowHead.tsx and the door in lib/sound/arrange.ts (another context), M
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
node probe:
[{"key":"g:Ambient","name":"Ambient","orphan":false},{"key":"g:ambient","name":"ambient","orphan":true},{"key":"∅","name":null,"orphan":false}]
{"ok":false,"error":"“ambient” is already a row"}
packages/ui/src/components/audio/arrange.ts:104-105
packages/ui/src/components/audio/arrangeGroups.ts:285
packages/ui/src/components/audio/RowHead.tsx:127
instrument: arrange.test case: rowsFor(["Ambient"], [take group "ambient"]) then the orphan's adopt through applyGroupOp + carriedBy + rowsFor again -> orphan rows 1 -> 0 and the take filed under "Ambient"; plus tests/next-server/audio-arrange.test.ts driving the door

title: Audition ←/→ sticks on a heard take that cannot play
body:
## Summary
stepTake returns a heard leaf's head take even when it has no bytes (src null) or is missing from the takes map; the island then does nothing, so the step can never pass that take.

## Description
stepTake (packages/ui/src/components/audio/HuntAudition.tsx:211-220) walks every heard leaf's headTake. HuntAudition itself skips a leaf whose take is undefined (HuntAudition.tsx:234) and draws no play for src null (:240), but the island's step (app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/Hunt.tsx:80-84) only plays when `t !== undefined && t.src !== null`: from the take before an unplayable one, → returns the unplayable id on every press and the transport never moves. Fixed: stepTake takes the takes map (or a playable predicate) and skips what cannot play; the island passes hunt.takes.

## Flow
- a hunt with heard leaves a (take src null) and b (playable); b playing
- press → : stepTake(heard, "t-b", 1) -> "t-a"; Hunt.tsx:83 sees src null and does nothing
- press → again: same id, same nothing - the step is stuck

## Expected impact
An operator auditioning with the keys can step through every playable take; today one file-less take walls off the rest in that direction. Could break: the wrap order of stepTake's existing case (hunt.test 'the audition').

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every step lands on a take that plays
Before: walked from the code: from b, presses of → that reach a playable take 0 of N
After: predicted N of N with playable-only ids
Method: simulation - the island is app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/Hunt.tsx, owned by the sibling context audio-hunt this wave; the stepTake half alone changes nothing the operator sees
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/ui/src/components/audio/HuntAudition.tsx:211-220 (ids of every heard head)
app/(studio)/audio/_hunt/Hunt.tsx:81-83 `const id = stepTake(heard, transport.playing, by); ... if (t !== undefined && t.src !== null) transport.toggle(...)`
instrument: hunt.test case: stepTake over [a (src null), b] with the takes map -> from t-b, → returns t-b (or the next playable), never t-a; red today

title: patchHunt accepts a parentId cycle the map then has to cut
body:
## Summary
The hunt door checks that a node's parent exists but not that the parents form a tree, so a PATCHed map can carry a cycle; dfca616b made the map draw it, the server still stores it and still calls every cycle node a parent.

## Description
lib/sound/hunt.ts:427-428 refuses a parentId missing from the map and nothing else. A cycle is stored as sent; buildTree now cuts it for drawing (dfca616b), but huntRender.leavesOf (lib/sound/huntRender.ts:179-182) builds `parents` from every parentId, so every node on a cycle is a parent there and a drawn leaf of a cut cycle is refused "is not a leaf of this hunt" at render. Fixed: the door refuses a cycle with a 400 naming the node, like the missing-parent case.

## Flow
- PATCH /hunts/<id> with nodes p(parent q), q(parent p)
- stored: 200
- map: p cut to a top, q drawn as a leaf (after dfca616b)
- Render q -> leavesOf refuses "q is not a leaf of this hunt"

## Expected impact
A cycle never reaches the store, so the map's cut is a guard rather than the normal path. Could break: a client that sends a map with a cycle today gets a 400 instead of a stored map.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the door refuses what the drawn map has to repair
Before: cycles refused by patchHunt 0 of 1 (read from lib/sound/hunt.ts:427-428)
After: predicted 1 of 1
Method: simulation - lib/sound/hunt.ts is outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
lib/sound/hunt.ts:427-428 `for (const n of next) if (n.parentId && !ids.has(n.parentId)) throw new SoundError(...)`
lib/sound/huntRender.ts:179 `const parents = new Set(hunt.nodes.map((n) => n.parentId));`
instrument: tests/next-server hunt patch case: a 2-cycle PATCH -> 400 naming the node; red today

title: One file-drop shape for the hunt's return and Arrange's round trip
body:
## Summary
ReturnDrop (HuntMap) and Drop (RoundTrip) are one native-file-drop component written twice, and the two CSS modules repeat nine rule-sets for it and the play button.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/audio/HuntMap.tsx:46-79 and packages/ui/src/components/audio/RoundTrip.tsx:302-337 are the same label + dragover/leave/drop + hidden file input, differing only in the label text. packages/ui/src/components/audio/Hunt.module.css:58-61,75-79 and packages/ui/src/components/audio/Arrange.module.css:32-35,47-51 repeat .play, .play:focus-visible, .playOn, .playMark, .drop, .drop:hover/.drop:focus-within, .dropOver, .dropBusy, .dropInput. CLAUDE.md: a shape spelled twice belongs in @gt/ui once, with its specimen on /kit. Fixed: one FileDrop (and the play button) in @gt/ui with a specimen, both callers on it.

## Flow
- count duplicated components: 2; duplicated rule-sets across the two modules: 9
- extract FileDrop with label/name/busy/onFile; move the rules once
- HuntMap and RoundTrip render it; hunt.test and arrange.test unchanged and green

## Expected impact
One place to fix a drop's behaviour (e.g. a busy guard) instead of two. Could break: the hunt drop is flex:1 and h-control-sm, Arrange's h-control - a size prop must keep both.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one drop implementation
Before: 2 components, 9 duplicated rule-sets
After: predicted 1 component, 0 duplicated rule-sets
Method: probe for Before (grep of the two modules); After not taken - a new @gt/ui shape with a specimen is M and touches /kit (outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A row rename that was opened cannot be abandoned
body:
## Summary
RowHead's rename field has no Escape and no blur exit: once open, the only way out is to submit, unchanged.

## Description
NameForm (packages/ui/src/components/audio/RowHead.tsx:83-96) handles submit only; RowHead closes the rename only in onDone (:117-120). Escape does nothing and focus leaving the field leaves it open, so a rename opened by mistake stays until Enter is pressed. Fixed: Escape (and blur with an unchanged value) close it without an edit.

## Flow
- press rename on a row
- press Escape -> the field stays
- click elsewhere -> the field stays
- only Enter closes it

## Expected impact
A mistaken rename press costs one key, not a submit. Could break: the keymap's FIELD_ATTR target handling if Escape is also a board verb.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a rename can be abandoned
Before: exits from an open rename other than submit 0 of 2 (read from the code)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - vitest runs with environment node (vitest.config.mts) and no DOM library is installed, so no case can press a key; the live lane is the director's
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a tests/live arrange case: open rename, press Escape -> the row name is drawn again and no groups edit was sent

title: The audition crowns a take with none of its brief in sight
body:
## Summary
HuntAudition is where the crown is given, but it draws only the leaf's axis, label, provider and the take's length - not the tempo, key, loop or length the leaf asked for.

## Description
media-generation/generated-music-acceptance, technique brief-conformance-listen: the first listen answers 'is this the piece that was briefed?', with the checklist derived from the brief so the brief keeps custody of the question. HuntAudition's header says the verdict is given where the takes are heard (packages/ui/src/components/audio/HuntAudition.tsx:180-185), yet the row (:236-255) carries no asked tempo/key/length - those are on the map card (HuntMap.tsx:105-111), a scroll away. Fixed: each audition take carries the leaf's asked commitments beside the measured length (asked length vs measured, bpm, key, loop), as chips.

## Flow
- open a hunt with heard leaves
- the audition row: axis, label, provider, measured length, Crown
- the asked 30 s / 78 bpm / D minor is on the map card only

## Expected impact
The crown is judged against what was asked, the technique's whole point. Could break: audition tile width at --w-tile-audio with four more chips.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - brief commitments visible where the verdict is given
Before: asked commitments drawn on the audition 0 of 4 (length, bpm, key, loop)
After: predicted 4 of 4 (those the leaf carries)
Method: simulation - a markup case can count it, but which commitments and in what shape is a layout call on a dense tile; a worker builds and photographs it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: hunt.test markup case: each audition take draws its leaf's asked length/bpm/key/loop chips (0 of 4 -> 4 of 4) plus a cx-capture of audio-hunt at 1920
